x: In the 5 miles’ walk, which was billed as an attempt on the world’s record, Roland Hardy, of Sheffield United Harriers, was pulled out and the rest of the field never looked like getting near the record.
236 lined up for the start and Vickers and Hall were seen to be well placed shortly afterwards behind Hardy, Coleman, Hawkins, Poole and others.
Roland Hardy soon showed that he was in excellent form and just went on increasing his lead throughout to win the race over a very fast course in a best Championship time.

Belgrave men, it seemed, were everywhere, and if all had been eligible to score we would have won the team event; as it was we missed third place by one point and were only eight points behind Metropolitan Walking Club, the winners. George Coleman added to his list of triumphs and missed the course record held by R.
Saturday started with a British record in the 7 miles walk of 50:11.6 by Roland Hardy of Sheffield closely followed by his team mate Lol Allen.
The disqualification of Roland Hardy and Lol Allen in their heats was most disappointing. However, George Coleman walked well in the final to finish 5th to Mikaelson of Sweden.
The event was won by Roland Hardy but to the surprise of everyone else Percy finished second. As he said the result of a race always depends on who turns up on the day!
